questions.stem: What does Fabric mirroring do with a supported operational database?

options.text: It moves the database into a Fabric warehouse and shuts down the source
It makes a one-time backup of the database in OneLake
It caches query results from the source in Power BI
It keeps a near real-time replica of the database's tables in OneLake as Delta tables

questions.explanation: Mirroring continuously replicates the source's data into OneLake in Delta format, so it can be analyzed in Fabric without building ETL pipelines.

questions.stem: Which three sources can Fabric mirroring replicate? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
questions.explanation: Azure SQL Database, Snowflake and Azure Cosmos DB are among the databases mirroring supports. File shares and semantic models aren't mirroring sources.

questions.stem: After a database is mirrored into Fabric, how can analysts query the replica with T-SQL?

options.text: Only by connecting to the source database
Through the mirrored database's SQL analytics endpoint
They can't; the replica is visible only to Spark

questions.explanation: A mirrored database comes with a SQL analytics endpoint for read-only T-SQL queries over the replicated tables.

questions.stem: You need a continuously updated copy of an Azure SQL database in OneLake, with as little to build and maintain as possible and no transformation on the way. What should you use?

options.text: A pipeline with a Copy activity scheduled every five minutes
A Spark notebook polling the source

questions.explanation: Mirroring is set up once and keeps the replica current with no pipelines or schedules to maintain. Pipelines and notebooks suit loads that need transformation or a source mirroring doesn't support.
